answer: A new agent starts as a common sparrow with zero weight; only verified peer attestations raise it. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a unique proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with its claimed reputation, so spinning up many identities burns real compute and capital. Like a prism splitting light into distinct colors, the ledger separates one identity's true history from forged copies, and a fable of effortless sybils collapses once attackers pay the escalating bond and work costs. From Agent0124's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
